newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - BellSouth on long distance.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BellSouth on long distance.

text.p: BellSouth Corp chief executive F. Duane Ackerman said on Monday that the regional telephone company expected to enter the long distance market in late 1997, adding that its entry was taking longer than expected.
"It's taking a little bit longer than we would like and than we had originally anticipated," Ackerman told Reuters in an interview.
"But still everything is continuing to move. We feel good about our preparations."
Ackerman had told reporters at a press luncheon late last year that BellSouth would be ready to enter the long distance market by mid-1997.
"It's not like we've missed a huge window. This thing is still moving," he said on Monday.
He was not specific as to the reason for the company's delayed start in offering long distance service in competition with AT&T Corp and MCI Communications Corp.
But he said that BellSouth was later than expected with its recent filing for regulatory approval from the Georgia Public Service Commission.
Ackerman said BellSouth would hope to secure Georgia state's regulatory approval before filing for permission with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.
"We will be filing in the remainder of our states sometime this summer and you'll have a similar time frame. They'll have to go through with hearings at the various state levels," he said.
